add-remove.title: Add/Remove
add-remove.description: Dynamically add and remove elements from the page
add-remove.information: As well as being able to dynamically add and remove elements from the page, you can also add `?initialElements=X` onto the url to generate elements on load.

autocomplete.title: Autocomplete
autocomplete.description: Pick a value from suggestions that appear as you type.
autocomplete.information: Start typing in either box to see suggestions. Use the up and down arrow keys to move through them (they wrap round), Enter to choose the highlighted one, or click a suggestion; Escape closes the list and a second Escape clears the box. Tabbing away closes the list without choosing anything, and changing the text after choosing clears the choice. The input follows the ARIA combobox pattern: aria-expanded says whether the list is open and aria-activedescendant points at the highlighted option, which has aria-selected="true". Suggestions match anywhere in a name, ignoring case and accents, with names that start with what you typed listed first, and the matching part is in bold. The country box filters a fixed list straight away. The city box asks a slow pretend server instead: it waits for at least {{min}} characters and a {{debounce}}ms pause in typing, shows a loading message while it waits, returns at most {{max}} cities, and answers short searches more slowly than long ones, so an old answer can arrive after a new one; only the answer for the current text is shown.

city.title: Cities (slow server)
city.slow-notice: Suggestions come from a slow pretend server, so they take up to {{wait}}ms to appear after you stop typing.
city.label: City

challenging-selectors.title: Challenging Selectors
challenging-selectors.description: Random IDs, identical buttons, split text and hidden duplicates that break naïve selectors.
challenging-selectors.information: This page is built so that the obvious selectors fail. The IDs and class names in the first section (and the class names elsewhere) are random hashes, like those from CSS-in-JS libraries, and change every time the page loads, so find the field by its label and the buttons by their role and name instead. The team table is shuffled on every load and every row has the same Edit and Delete buttons with no accessible name of their own, so pick the row by its content (the person's name or email) and then the button inside that row; a row position or nth match will hit someone else. The greeting and unread message count are split across several elements, so a match on an element's own text will not find the whole sentence: match on the text of the parent, or normalise the text first. The marking button's label is split the same way, but its accessible name is still the full sentence. The two address blocks have fields whose labels are plain text that is not tied to the inputs, and the two blocks are identical apart from their title, so you have to locate a field relative to the nearby text or by its position inside the right block. The two newsletter forms do the same thing: the labelled one has a heading, a label, a real button and data-testid attributes, while the unlabelled one only has a placeholder, a clickable div styled like a button and random class names, so compare how each locator strategy copes with both. Finally, the Checkout button is in the page three times: a mobile and a desktop version, of which only one is shown depending on the screen width, and a third inside the closed More options panel, so a locator has to target the visible one rather than the first one in the DOM. The Last action panel at the top shows what your last click actually did, so you can check you hit the element you meant to.

addresses.title: Fields told apart by nearby text

date-picker.title: Date Picker
date-picker.description: A custom calendar date picker: single dates, disabled days, a date range and a field you can type into or pick from.
date-picker.information: Each picker opens its calendar in a popup that is added at the end of the page's <body>, not next to its field, so look for it from the whole document rather than inside the field's container. There is no typing into the appointment or trip pickers: to reach a date in another month, use the previous and next month buttons or the month and year lists, and check which month is showing first. Which days can be picked depends on today's date, read from the browser's clock when the page opens, so a test that picks "next Monday" or "the 15th of this month" gets a different date (or a disabled one) on a different day unless the clock is faked. Disabled days are still shown and can be focused, but they are marked aria-disabled, struck through, and clicking them does nothing. Each day is a button whose text is just the day number, whose accessible name is the full date in the current language (e.g. "Friday, November 20, 2026") and which has a data-date attribute in ISO format. Appointments and trips can be booked up to the end of {{lastYear}}. The trip picker stays open after the first day and closes after the last; picking a day before the first starts again from there. The date of birth field follows the current language's format (MM/DD/YYYY in English, DD/MM/YYYY in French and Portuguese), so 03/04/2000 is 4 March in English but 3 April in French, and the text is only checked when Enter is pressed or the field loses focus; dates in the future or before {{minYear}} are refused. The week starts on Sunday in English and Portuguese and on Monday in French, so the same date is in a different column. Under each picker the chosen value is shown in ISO format (YYYY-MM-DD), the same in every language: assert on that rather than on the displayed text. In the calendar the arrow keys move by day and week, Page Up and Page Down by month, Home and End to the start and end of the week, Enter picks the focused day and Escape closes it.

drag-and-drop.description: Drag elements from one side of the page and drop them on the other side.
drag-and-drop.information: You able to drag an infinite amount of the red boxes and drop them on the grey box.

drag-and-drop-hard.description: Drag the appropriate smaller shapes onto the larger shape.
drag-and-drop-hard.information: A correct drop will result in the shape turning green, otherwise the shape will turn yellow. Note: the shapes change on each reload

dropdown.title: Dropdown
dropdown.description: Pick options from a native select, a multi-select and a custom dropdown.
dropdown.information: There are three kinds of dropdown here. The first two are native <select> elements, so most frameworks can choose an option directly by its value or text; the second allows several options to be picked at once. The third is a custom dropdown built from buttons and a list: it is not a <select>, and its options only exist in the DOM, at the end of the page, while it is open, so click it to open it and then click an option. Some options are disabled and cannot be picked. Your current choices are shown underneath.

dynamic-loading.title: Dynamic Loading
dynamic-loading.description: Elements that appear, disappear and change state after a random delay.
dynamic-loading.information: Each section changes the page after a random delay of between {{min}} and {{max}} seconds, picked again every time, so a fixed sleep is sometimes too short and always slower than needed: wait for the condition you actually need instead. The first section adds an element to the DOM only once its spinner finishes, so it cannot be found before then. The second has its element in the DOM from the start but hidden with display: none, so it is present long before it is visible. The third has an input that is disabled until the async step finishes, and clicking it while disabled does nothing. The fourth removes its checkbox and later adds a brand new one, so a reference to the old element goes stale and has to be looked up again. The last shows "Loading..." and then "Still loading..." before its final text, so waiting only for "Loading..." to go away is not enough: wait for the text you expect.

dynamic-table.information: Note: the table data refreshes on a reload.

form-validation.information: Errors appear when you leave a field and when you submit the form. Phone and website are optional but must be valid if filled in. Age must be a whole number between 18 and 120. The password needs at least 8 characters with an uppercase letter, a lowercase letter and a number.

geolocation.title: Geolocation
geolocation.description: Find the browser's location, then follow it as it moves.
geolocation.information: The browser asks for permission before sharing its location, and that prompt is not part of the page, so grant (or deny) the geolocation permission and set a fake location in your test framework before clicking. "Get my location" reads the position once; "Start watching" keeps following it, so change the fake location and the page will update. The coordinates, their accuracy and the nearest of a few well known cities are shown underneath. If permission is denied, the position cannot be found or it takes too long, an error explains why.

hovers.title: Hovers
hovers.description: Interact with elements that only appear while the mouse is over something.
hovers.information: Everything on this page only shows up while the mouse pointer rests on something, so tests have to hover first. The details on each profile card are not in the DOM at all until the card is hovered, and on purpose there is no other way to reveal them. The buttons on each file are always in the DOM but stay invisible until their row is hovered, so a test that clicks them straight away will be told they are not visible; keyboard users can also reveal them by tabbing to the row. The menu opens its submenus a moment after an item is hovered and closes a moment after the pointer leaves it, so move through it the way a person would; clicking an item opens its submenu straight away. The last thing you did is shown underneath.

iframes.title: IFrames
iframes.description: Forms, nested frames and a rich text editor that live inside iframes, so you have to switch into a frame to reach them.
iframes.information: Everything inside an iframe belongs to a separate document, so selectors run on the page cannot find it: tests have to switch into the frame first, and back out again to check anything on the page. The form sends its message to the page outside the frame. The counter sits inside a frame that is itself inside another frame, so it takes two switches to reach. The rich text editor works like many classic WYSIWYG editors: the text you edit is the body of a frame, while its toolbar, word count and HTML output are on the page around it, so a test has to move between the two.

infinite-scroll.information: Scroll to the end of the list to load the next batch of 10 items. A loading indicator is shown for a moment before the new items appear, and the feed never runs out, so wait for the new items rather than for the end of the list.

js-alerts.title: JS Alerts
js-alerts.description: Handle the browser's native alert, confirm and prompt dialogs, which are not part of the page.
js-alerts.information: Each button opens one of the browser's built-in JavaScript dialogs. They are drawn by the browser rather than the page, so they cannot be found in the DOM: listen for the dialog, check its message, then accept or dismiss it (typing an answer into the prompt first). The result of your choice is shown on the page once the dialog closes.

key-presses.title: Key Presses
key-presses.description: Interact with the page by pressing keys on the keyboard.
key-presses.information: Everything on this page is driven by the keyboard, so tests have to send key presses rather than click or type text. The key reader shows the last key pressed in its text box, with its key and code and any modifier keys held with it, plus the last few keys pressed. The counter only changes while it has focus: the up and down (or right and left) arrow keys move it by 1, holding Shift moves it by 10, Home and End jump to the lowest and highest values and Escape puts it back where it started. The hold control only confirms if Space is held down for a whole second; letting go sooner does not count, and holding a key down repeats its keydown event, so each repeat has to be ignored. There is no mouse alternative on purpose.

reader.label: Press any key in this box

counter.label: Counter
counter.instructions: Focus the counter, then use the arrow keys to change it. Hold Shift to move in steps of 10. Home and End jump to 0 and 100, and Escape resets it to 50.

modal-dialogs.title: Modal Dialogs
modal-dialogs.description: Open, use and close dialogs drawn in the page, including one that appears by itself on load.
modal-dialogs.information: Unlike the browser's native dialogs (see JS Alerts), these modals are ordinary DOM elements, but each is rendered in its own element at the end of <body>, outside the scenario's markup, so look for it from the document rather than inside the section that opened it. While a modal is open a full-screen backdrop sits over the page and everything behind it is marked inert and aria-hidden="true": clicks on the page are intercepted by the backdrop and background elements drop out of the accessibility tree, so role-based queries no longer find them. The basic modal closes with its close button, the Escape key or a click on the backdrop, and reports which one was used. The confirmation modal guards a delete: the safe Cancel button gets focus, and Escape or the backdrop also cancel. The form modal keeps focus trapped inside while it is open (Tab wraps around) and gives focus back to the button that opened it when it closes. The stacked modals show a second dialog on top of the first: Escape and the backdrop only close the top one. Finally, a welcome modal opens by itself on your first visit and can only be closed with its button; that choice is remembered in localStorage under modal-dialogs-entry-dismissed, so tests must either dismiss it or set that key before the page loads.

mouse-interactions.title: Mouse Interactions
mouse-interactions.description: Double-click, right-click, click and hold, and click with different mouse buttons and modifier keys.
mouse-interactions.information: Every target on this page needs more than a plain left click, and each testing tool exposes these mouse actions differently. The double-click target ignores single clicks and only counts double-clicks. The note opens a custom context menu on right-click instead of the browser's own one, and its items pin, highlight or delete the note; the menu is a separate element positioned where the pointer was, and it closes on Escape or when you press anywhere outside it. The hold button only confirms if the left mouse button is held down on it for a whole second, so the press and release have to be sent as separate steps with a wait in between; letting go or moving off it sooner does not count, and the progress bar shows how far through the hold you are. The last box reports which mouse button was pressed (left, middle, right, back or forward) and which modifier keys (Shift, Control, Alt, Meta) were held at the time. The panel at the top always shows the last interaction. There is no keyboard alternative for the double-click, hold or mouse button targets on purpose.

multiple-windows.title: Multiple Windows
multiple-windows.description: Links and buttons that open new tabs and popup windows, which tests have to switch to and back from.
multiple-windows.information: Every tab or window has a document of its own, so a test only sees the one it is focused on: it has to wait for the new window, switch to it, and switch back to the original afterwards. Each window sets its own document title to tell it apart. The popup sends a message back to the window that opened it, then closes itself, while the page keeps track of whether it is still open. The two named-window links both open in the same window, so clicking the second reuses it instead of opening another.

paginated-table.title: Paginated Table
paginated-table.description: Find invoices across the pages of a table with search, filters, row selection and a bulk action.
paginated-table.information: The table holds 143 invoices, shown 10, 25 or 50 at a time. Every change (a new page, page size, search or filter) loads for a random {{min}} to {{max}} ms, and while it loads the old rows stay on screen: the table is marked aria-busy="true", an overlay with a spinner covers it and the pager, page size and checkboxes are disabled. Checking the rows straight after a click can read the old page, so wait for the load to finish or for the row count summary to change. The search box only searches once typing has paused for {{debounce}} ms, and then loads again; it matches the invoice number or the customer, ignoring case and accents ("cafe" finds "Café Étoile"). A new search, filter or page size goes back to page 1, and both ends of the date range are included. The pager shows the first and last pages and those either side of the current one, with … for the rest, so the page you want may not have a button yet; the current page is marked aria-current="page". Selected rows stay selected when you change page or filter, even when they are no longer shown, and the selected count includes them. The checkbox in the header only selects the rows on the current page, and is partly checked when only some of them are. Marking invoices as paid changes them straight away, so with a status filter on they can disappear from the page. When nothing matches, the table shows a message with a button to clear the filters, and the pager is removed. The summary, dates and amounts are worded and formatted differently in each language.

radio-button.description: A set of radio buttons to check against.
radio-button.information: Depending on the first radio button clicked, a second set will appear and change based on the first one clicked.

shadow-dom.title: Shadow DOM
shadow-dom.description: Elements hidden inside open, nested and closed shadow roots, so you can check how your tools reach into the shadow DOM.
shadow-dom.information: Regular selectors stop at a shadow root boundary. The open shadow root can be pierced by most tools, the nested example needs two hops, the slotted content lives in the light DOM even though it is shown inside a shadow root, and the closed shadow root cannot be reached through host.shadowRoot at all.

sortable-table.title: Sortable Table
sortable-table.description: Sort a table by clicking its column headers.
sortable-table.information: Click a column header to sort by it: the first click sorts ascending, the second descending and the third puts the rows back in their original order. The sorted column's header says which way it is sorted in its aria-sort attribute, and the other headers have none; the Email column cannot be sorted. The values are picked to catch naive sorting: salaries and project counts sort wrongly as text, start dates are shown in your language's format, one name starts with an accented letter, and several people share a department (they keep their original order when tied). The contractor has no salary and always sorts last, whichever way the column is sorted. The current sort is shown underneath the table.
